title: Animals in Expressions
text:
Animal idioms have passed into everyday speech so thoroughly that few speakers consider their origins. To let the cat out of the bag once meant revealing a secret, perhaps because a cat sold in a sack was often a trick played on buyers. Such phrases carry knowledge about past markets, farms and households, even when the original context has vanished.

Other animal idioms are harder to explain. Expressions like raining cats and dogs have been traced to medieval England, but the exact link to animals is uncertain. Historians caution that a plausible story is not necessarily a true one, and that many explanations were proposed long after the idioms themselves had become common.

questions.text: According to paragraph one, what did 'to let the cat out of the bag' once mean?
According to paragraph two, which idiom has been traced to medieval England?
options: Let the cat out of the bag

questions.text: What can be inferred about the explanation for raining cats and dogs?
options: The link to animals is uncertain
It was invented in the twentieth century

questions.text: What does the writer suggest about the explanations proposed for idioms?
options: They were proposed before the idioms became common
They were often proposed long after the idioms became common

vocabulary.definition: seeming reasonable or likely to be true
relating to the period of European history roughly from 500 to 1500

paragraph_translations: As expressões com animais se incorporaram tanto à fala cotidiana que poucos falantes pensam em suas origens. Antigamente, to let the cat out of the bag significava revelando um segredo, talvez porque um gato vendido dentro de um saco fosse muitas vezes uma armadilha para os compradores. Essas expressões carregam conhecimento sobre antigos mercados, fazendas e lares, mesmo quando o contexto original desapareceu.

Outras expressões com animais são mais difíceis de explicar. Frases como raining cats and dogs foram rastreadas até a Inglaterra medieval, mas a ligação exata com os animais é incerta. Historiadores alertam que uma história plausível não é necessariamente verdadeira, e que muitas explicações foram propostas muito depois de as expressões já terem se tornado comuns.
